title: Mitigate credential-epoch bleed causing billing/rate-limit misattribution during subaccount rollouts
creator: Alyssa Chen
description:
Summary: After a staged rollout of service-credential rotations for a subset of subaccounts, we observed transient double-counting of request tokens and incorrect owner attribution in the metering pipeline. Symptoms include: unexpected billing spikes for parent orgs, per-token latency regressions in rate-limiter logs, and quota exhaustion alerts for unaffected projects. This ticket traces a race between ingress claim assignment and the metering/rate-limiter owner lookup when credentials are rotated in-place across subaccounts.

Incident timeline & observable signals:
- 2025-02-09 03:14 UTC: first billing spike alert on billing-prod for org org-8892 (dashboards showed +12% tokens compared to baseline).
- Ingress logs show requests arriving with two different credential epochs within ~700ms windows. Header observed: X-Auth-Epoch with values "epoch:421" and "epoch:422".
- Metering-aggregator emitted entries mapping some tokens to parent-org and some to subaccount, for the same contiguous request stream.
- Rate-limiter counters (rl-frontend) incremented owner-mapped buckets for both the pre-rotation and post-rotation owner IDs, leading to quick quota hits for unrelated projects.

Reproduction steps:
1. In staging, rotate service-credential for subaccount S-77 using the phased deploy tool (rollout window 2s, rotation commit).
2. Replay 10k requests over a 1s interval via loadtest that reuses short-lived JWTs generated by the old and new credential versions.
3. Observe metering-aggregator attribution and rate-limiter bucket attribution divergence in logs under 1s windows.

Root cause hypothesis (current):
- The ingress authentication path updates a per-worker claim-cache during credential epoch swap but does the update in two non-atomic steps: (1) insert new mapping, (2) delete old mapping. If requests surface between these ops and a background reconciliation runs, metering and rate-limiter pipelines receive inconsistent tenant IDs.
- Metering-aggregator and rate-limiter lookup flow rely on claim-cache TTL eviction + eventual consistency; they do not carry the credential epoch along the request path, so they cannot deterministically pick the correct owner during transient state.

Proposed fixes and mitigations:
- Short term (hotfix): add a per-request routing header X-Auth-Epoch forwarded from ingress to downstream metering and rate-limiter services so they can deterministically resolve owner by preferring mappings that match the epoch. Deploy to staging and one canary region for 24 hours.
- Medium term: make claim-cache updates atomic by swapping the new shard in and removing the old mapping in a single compare-and-swap operation. This includes adding an epoch field to the canonical tenant claim and enforcing monotonic epoch checks on write.
- Long term: add a deterministic owner-selection algorithm in the metering-aggregator that prefers explicit (credential, epoch) bindings over name-based heuristics during rolling changes, and add a reconciliation job that replays 1 minute of ingress envelopes on mismatch to patch retroactive attributions.

Validation criteria:
- No dual-attribution observed in a 1-hour rolling load test with credential rotations at 2s granularity in staging.
- Billing dashboards in canary region show no unexplained token increases during test windows.
- Rate-limiter unit tests for owner mapping cover epoch gaps and concurrent lookups.

Monitoring & rollout plan:
- Deploy hotfix of X-Auth-Epoch header forwarding to ingress, metering-aggregator, and rate-limiter on canary (10% traffic) -> monitor 6h -> increase to 50% -> 100% if stable.
- Instrument new histograms: owner-attribution-latency, epoch-mismatch-count, dual-attribution-events.
- Postmortem if dual-attribution > 0 after full rollout.

Artifacts & links:
- Loadtest scripts: https://github.com/redwood/loadtests/tree/main/credential-epoch-replay
- Initial investigation notes and sample logs: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-investigation-notes (internal)
- Draft PR for epoch header forwarding: https://github.com/redwood/ingress/pull/8142
- Proposed atomic cache patch: https://github.com/redwood/claim-cache/pull/129
